title: An array of exactly maxArraySize elements is not truncated
rationale: The cliff edge from below for maxArraySize. Math.min makes size==limit safe, but nothing states that as a contract; a change to a strict comparison would silently drop the last element of every array sitting exactly at the bound.
catchesBugClass: Off-by-one at the array bound - the same silent-shape-change risk as depth-exactly-max, and it would corrupt only the population least likely to appear in ad-hoc testing.
cannotCatch: Identical input to the below-max fixture, so it can only catch a regression in the COMPARISON, never in element handling. Paired with array-size-one-over-max it brackets the cliff; alone it proves very little.

predicted.detail: limit = min(3,3) = 3, all elements retained, identical behaviour to the below-max fixture.
